'''''The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay''''' is a [[first-person shooter]] and [[Stealth game|stealth]] video game developed by [[Starbreeze Studios]] and [[Tigon Studios]] and published by [[Vivendi Universal Games]]. Released for the [[Xbox (console)|Xbox]] and [[Microsoft Windows]] in 2004, the game's story is a [[prequel]] to the futuristic [[science fiction]] film ''[[Pitch Black (film)|Pitch Black]]''. Actor [[Vin Diesel]]—who was involved in the game's development—reprises his role as that film's protagonist, [[Richard B. Riddick]].

The game follows Riddick, the anti-hero of the two films ''[[Pitch Black (film)|Pitch Black]]'' and ''[[The Chronicles of Riddick]]'', as he attempts to escape from a maximum-security prison called Butcher Bay. ''Escape from Butcher Bay''{{'}}s designers focused on exploring Riddick's character in a prison break setting to differentiate the game from the film.  The game's influences include the film ''[[Escape from Alcatraz (film)|Escape from Alcatraz]]'', and video games such as ''[[Half-Life (video game)|Half-Life]]'', ''[[Thief: The Dark Project]]'', and ''[[Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell (video game)|Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell]]''.

''Escape from Butcher Bay'' received acclaim by critics, who lauded its graphics and its implementation of stealth, action and adventure elements. Some critics consider the game superior to the film, a rarity among film tie-in games. However, they commonly lamented its brevity and lack of multiplayer components. The game is cited as one of the [[List of video games considered the best|greatest video games ever made]]. It went on to win several accolades, including the [[Golden Joystick Award]] for Unsung Hero Game of the Year and the [[Spike Video Game Award]] for Best Game Based on a Movie. In 2009, the game was included in ''[[The Chronicles of Riddick: Assault on Dark Athena]]'', with enhanced visuals.

==Gameplay==
[[File:CREBBSneak.jpg|thumb|left|alt=A pair of human arms with brown tape on them holding a screwdriver in the right hand. A man working on a machine, wearing a green jumpsuit and a black shirt, is in front of the arms with blood splatter on the wall to his left.|Riddick in stealth mode, preparing to stab an enemy with a screwdriver]]
In ''Escape from Butcher Bay'', the player takes control of protagonist [[Richard B. Riddick]] as he attempts to break out of Butcher Bay prison.<ref name="1uppcreview" /> The game incorporates various elements from [[video game genres]] such as [[first-person shooter]], [[Adventure game|adventure]] and [[Stealth game|stealth]],<ref name="gspotxboxreview2" /><ref name="gspotxboxreview" /> and is played primarily from a [[First person (video games)|first-person perspective]], though the camera switches to a [[Virtual camera system|third-person perspective]] during certain scenes.<ref name="gspotxboxreview3" /> Unlike many first-person shooters, the game contains no [[HUD (video gaming)|head-up display]];<ref name="gspotxboxreview2" /><ref name="oxmlicense">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.oxmonline.com/article/xbox-soapbox/licensed-games?page=0,1|title=Defending Licensed Games|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081123193820/http://www.oxmonline.com/article/xbox-soapbox/licensed-games?page=0%2C1|archive-date=November 23, 2008|last=Dyer|first=Mitch|date=August 12, 2008|magazine=Official Xbox Magazine|access-date=April 5, 2009}}</ref> on-screen cues are limited to flashes when a new weapon is selected,<ref name="cvgpcreview" /> and small, white boxes that display the [[player character]]'s [[Health (gaming)|health]] when damage is taken.<ref name="1uppcreview" /> Health can be replenished in designated areas throughout the game.<ref name="ignxboxpreview2">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/01/27/the-chronicles-of-riddick-3?page=2|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Preview|page=2|last=Boulding|first=Aaron|date=January 26, 2004|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305193509/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/01/27/the-chronicles-of-riddick-3?page=2|archive-date=March 5, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> By finding cigarette packs hidden in [[Level (video games)|levels]], the player can unlock concept art and video files.<ref name="cvgxboxreview" />

The player may interact with and receive [[Quest (gaming)|quests]] from the prison's residents,<ref name="europcreview" /> and earns information, tools and other rewards by completing quests.<ref name="gzpcreview" /> Violent conflict often occurs between the player, inmates and prison guards.<ref name="1uppcreview" /><ref name="europcreview" /> The player attacks with Riddick's bare hands, or with improvised weapons such as [[Shiv (weapon)|shivs]] and [[Club (weapon)|clubs]]. [[Combo (gaming)|Combos]] are created by stringing together punches.<ref name="gspotxboxreview2" /><ref name="cvgpcreview" /><ref name="ignxboxreview2">{{cite web|url=http://xbox.ign.com/articles/519/519763p2.html|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review|page=2|work=[[IGN]]|last=Perry|first=Douglass C.|date=May 28, 2004|publisher=Ziff Davis|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305163410/http://xbox.ign.com/articles/519/519763p2.html|archive-date=March 5, 2012}}</ref> A DNA-scanning security system initially prevents Riddick from using firearms, but a limited arsenal later becomes available.<ref name="gspotxboxreview2" /><ref name="cvgpcreview" /><ref name="gspyxboxreview" />

A "stealth mode" is activated when the [[player character]] crouches, allowing the player to move silently and tinting the edges of the screen blue when the player is hidden.<ref name="gspotxboxreview3" /> While in stealth mode, the player can drag bodies out of sight and hide from enemies.<ref name="gspotxboxreview3" /><ref name="gzpcreview" /> The mode grants attacks that quickly kill enemies;<ref name="gspyxboxreview" /> the player may drop on enemies from above, or execute them from behind.<ref name="1uppcreview" /><ref name="gspyxboxreview" /> During the game, Riddick acquires ''[[Tapetum lucidum|eyeshine]]'', allowing him to see in the dark but temporarily blinding him if used in brightly lit areas.<ref name="cvgpcreview" /><ref name="palgnxboxreview" />

==Plot==

===Setting and characters===
''Escape from Butcher Bay'' is set in the futuristic [[science fiction]] universe of the [[The Chronicles of Riddick (franchise)|''Chronicles of Riddick'' franchise]],<ref name="gzpcreview" /> and is a prequel to the film ''[[Pitch Black (film)|Pitch Black]]''.<ref name="gspotpress" /> The game takes place inside Butcher Bay, a [[Types of US federal prisons|maximum-security]] prison from which no prisoner has escaped.<ref name="1uppcreview" /><ref name="gspotxboxreview" /> The facility—constructed on a barren planet—contains three increasingly secure holding areas, and a subterranean mining operation.<ref name="ignxboxreview2" />

The game's [[Player character|protagonist]] is Richard B. Riddick (reprised by [[Vin Diesel]]), a murderer recently confined in Butcher Bay.<ref name="cvgpcreview" /><ref name="gspyxboxreview" /> Riddick is resourceful, and seeks to break out of the prison by any means necessary.<ref name="gspotxboxreview" /> His capturer is the [[bounty hunter]] William J. Johns (reprised by [[Cole Hauser]]); the two have had previous encounters.<ref name="cvgpcreview" /> Butcher Bay's warden is a man named Hoxie ([[Dwight Schultz]]),<ref name="gspyxboxreview" /><ref name="euroxboxreview" /> while Abbott ([[Xzibit]]) is a prison guard disliked by the inmates.<ref name="1uppcreview" /><ref name="cvgxboxreview" /> The inmate Pope Joe ([[Willis Burks II]]) is an insane old man, who lives in the sewer tunnels beneath the prison.<ref name="cvgxboxreview" /><ref name="ignxboxreview5" />

===Story===
The opening cinematic shows Riddick in hiding, having grown out his hair and beard, before the opening scene of the ''Chronicles of Riddick'' movie. He hunts an animal and after killing it, a disembodied voice starts talking to him asking him where he got his eyes. He states that he received them from a "slam preacher" and this causes him to remember his time at Butcher Bay. The game takes place in a flashback.

Another opening cinematic takes place in which Riddick is being transported for collection on the bounty. He and Johns have a brief conversation in which Riddick tells Johns that there is no way he is going to get the price he wants. Riddick wakes up as they land and stands out front of Butcher Bay waiting for the warden. He sneaks up behind Johns and breaks his neck and proceeds to escape. After getting his hands on a gun, he goes through the ventilation ducts and seemingly escapes into the desert. Everything fades to white as Riddick hears Johns saying, "Rise and shine, Riddick." It turns out this escape was simply a dream.

Riddick wakes up and Johns escorts him off the ship. Johns meets with Hoxie to negotiate his pay,<ref name="gspyxboxreview" /> while Abbott escorts Riddick to his cell in the "single-max" security area. After making enemies with and killing a gang leader named Rust ([[Steve Blum]]), Riddick familiarizes himself with the facility, and soon instigates a riot; during the confusion, he escapes into the prison's sewer system. Armed with a shotgun and a dying flashlight, Riddick discovers he is not alone in the sewers. Fighting through the sewers against mutant "dwellers",<ref name="palgnxboxreview">{{cite web|url=http://palgn.com.au/article.php?id=1338|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review - Xbox Review|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120728231356/http://palgn.com.au/xbox/1338/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-review/|archive-date=July 28, 2012|author=Christophe|date=August 21, 2004|website=PALGN|access-date=April 5, 2009}}</ref> Riddick eventually meets Pope Joe, for whom he retrieves a lost radio, which Joe calls a blessed voicebox. A woman named Shirah ([[Kristin Lehman]])<ref name="ignxboxreview5" /> tells Riddick that he "has been blind too long", and he gains his trademark "eyeshine" night vision.<ref name="cvgxboxreview" /> Afterwards, he accuses Pope Joe of tampering with his eyes; Joe says that he merely treated Riddick's injured arm. Riddick then continues his escape, while using the eyeshine to his advantage.

After emerging from a manhole in the showers of the guard living quarters, Riddick uses a guard uniform to blend in as he makes his way to the space port and his chance at escape. Realizing he requires a guard to get through the retinal scanner that locks the doors to the space port, Riddick decides to go after Abbott and take his eyes. He gains access to Abbott's apartment by telling him there is a delivery for him. A fire fight ensues and after that, as Abbott bleeds out on the floor, Riddick moves in for the kill but is stopped by Johns.

Riddick is captured and transferred to the "double-max" security area. Gaining the trust of the inmates by participating in fighting matches, Riddick eventually kills the champion of the fighting matches, a guard named Bam. This leads him to be taken to a room where no surveillance is seen and several guards await to kill Riddick. Abbott walks into the room, fully healed, holding a baseball bat. Shirah returns to him and tells him that the fury of all of his kind is within him, and he can release it if he chooses. Riddick lets out a loud scream as a blast of energy called the 'Rage of Furya' kills all the guards around him except Abbott, who hides and then panics and attacks Riddick. Riddick kills Abbott, steals his keycard, and proceeds to find another way to escape. Using a secret entrance to an elevator, he infiltrates a mining facility. He meets an inmate of great influence in the area named Jagger Valance ([[Ron Perlman]]),<ref name="ignxboxreview5" /> who wishes to escape with him. He makes a bomb and plants it in a mining site with a massive gas leak. However, Riddick is discovered and caught by the guards. During his transfer to another section, the prison is disrupted by an outbreak of creatures called "Xeno", due to the bomb Riddick planted, in order to create the confusion necessary for his escape, and Riddick attempts to escape with Valance. His plans are foiled again by Johns. After a fist fight, Riddick and Johns are both shot by Valance (who only meant to hit Johns) and Valance is killed by the guards. After meeting again with the warden, and telling him that he is just getting started, Riddick is placed in the "triple-max" area, where inmates are kept in [[Cryonics|cryonic]] sleep.<ref name="ignxboxreview2" /> They are awakened daily for two minutes of exercise; during this time, Riddick discovers a flaw in the system and escapes. He then hijacks a large robot and fights his way through Butcher Bay to reach Hoxie.<ref name="gproxboxreview" />

Tired of dealing with the prison officials, Johns helps Riddick to elude the guards. Riddick knocks Johns out and flies the ship into the warden's office. The warden calls in two robot guards with cloaking abilities and Riddick defeats them. After Hoxie surrenders, Riddick receives the codes to Hoxie's ship and Riddick and Johns escape disguised as a guard and prisoner. Two guards enter Hoxie's room, where Hoxie is bound and covered in Riddick's former attire with a gun tied to him and aimed at the door. The guards mistake Hoxie for Riddick and kill him. Riddick and Johns take off in Hoxie's ship, ending the game.

In a closing cinematic, after recalling the events at Butcher Bay, Riddick is shown visions of the events to come in the ''Chronicles of Riddick'' and prepares himself.

==Development==
[[File:Vin Diesel by Gage Skidmore 2.jpg|thumb|right|alt=A bald, multi-racial man in a gray suit. Turned at a 45 degree angle from the camera, he squints in the direction of an off-camera light source, which illuminates his face.|Actor [[Vin Diesel]] reprised his role as Riddick for ''Escape from Butcher Bay'', and assisted in the game's development.]]
''Escape from Butcher Bay'' was co-developed by Swedish company [[Starbreeze Studios]] and the [[Vin Diesel]]-founded [[Tigon Studios]], and published by [[Vivendi Games]] and Tigon Studios. Universal Studios Consumer Products Group granted ''The Chronicles of Riddick'' license to Universal Interactive; both companies were owned by Vivendi Universal. The game was announced in March 2004 as an [[Xbox (console)|Xbox]] title. Tigon Studios' Cos Lazouras said, "[The game] features an original storyline that provides insight into how Riddick evolved into such a complex character".<ref name="gspotpress">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/xbox/action/chroniclesofriddick/printable_6091271.html/|title=VU Games Announces The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay|author=GameSpot Staff|date=November 3, 2004|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040904023133/http://www.gamespot.com/xbox/action/chroniclesofriddick/printable_6091271.html|archive-date=September 4, 2004}}</ref>

In contrast to other film [[tie-in]] games, which often closely follow the events of their source material, the development team of ''Escape from Butcher Bay'' focused on differentiating the game from ''The Chronicles of Riddick''.<ref name="ignsbint">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay|title=Epilogue: The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay|last=Perry|first=Douglass C.|page=1|date=September 1, 2004|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130306175856/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay|archive-date=March 6, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> They sought to explore Riddick's character in a [[Prison escape|prison break]] setting, and took inspiration from films such as ''[[Escape from Alcatraz (film)|Escape from Alcatraz]]''. Starbreeze was also inspired by video games such as ''[[GoldenEye 007 (1997 video game)|GoldenEye 007]]'' and the [[Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell|''Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell'' series]].<ref name="ignsbint6" /><ref name="ignsbint5">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-pt-2?page=2|title=Epilogue: The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay, Pt. 2|last=Perry|first=Douglass C.|page=2|date=September 2, 2004|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303125327/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-pt-2?page=2|archive-date=March 3, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> The opening sequence, in which Riddick is escorted into Butcher Bay,<ref name="ignintro">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/04/29/pre-e3-2004-the-chronicles-of-riddick-hands-on?page=2|title=Pre-E3 2004: The Chronicles of Riddick Hands-on|last1=Perry|first1=Douglass C.|last2=Goldstein|first2=Hilary|page=2|date=April 29, 2004|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160325164311/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/04/29/pre-e3-2004-the-chronicles-of-riddick-hands-on?page=2|archive-date=March 25, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> is a tribute to ''[[Half-Life (video game)|Half-Life]]'', the game's hand-to-hand combat was inspired by ''[[Punch-Out!!]]'',<ref name="ignsbint6">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-pt-2?page=3|title=Epilogue: The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay, Pt. 2|last=Perry|first=Douglass C.|page=3|date=September 2, 2004|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308005356/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-pt-2?page=3|archive-date=March 8, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> and the stealth mechanics, such as hiding in the shadows and leaning, were inspired by that of ''[[Thief: The Dark Project]]'' and ''[[Deus Ex]]''. Starbreeze focused solely on developing the game's [[Single-player video game|single-player]] mode, and did not include [[Multiplayer video game|multiplayer]]; the company believed that such a mode would require a design team twice as large and another year of development.<ref name="ignsbint5" /><ref name="ignsbint4">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-pt-2|title=Epilogue: The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay, Pt. 2|last=Perry|first=Douglass C.|page=1|date=September 2, 2004|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130306175902/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-pt-2|archive-date=March 6, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

Vin Diesel, the lead actor of ''The Chronicles of Riddick'', provided his voice and likeness for Riddick. He and director [[David Twohy]] also contributed to the game's plot and character design; the game's story was developed in conjunction with the film's.<ref name="gspottigon">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/qanda-tigon-studios-cos-lazouras/1100-6100596/|title=Q&A: Tigon Studios' Cos Lazouras|last=Feldman|first=Curt|date=June 12, 2004|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131206032039/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/qanda-tigon-studios-cos-lazouras/1100-6100596/|archive-date=December 6, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> Per the filmmakers' instructions, the designers made the origin of Riddick's "eyeshine" vague.<ref name="ignsbint3">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay?page=3|title=Epilogue: The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay (page 3)|last=Perry|first=Douglass C.|page=3|date=September 1, 2004|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-date=June 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210620201710/https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay?page=3|url-status=live}}</ref> Diesel offered guidance to the game's lead writer during voice recording sessions; this included dialogue rewrites to reduce Riddick's lines, as Diesel believed the character spoke too often.<ref name="ignsbint2">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay?page=2|title=Epilogue: The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay|last=Perry|first=Douglass C.|page=2|date=September 1, 2004|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-date=June 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210620081309/https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay?page=2|url-status=live}}</ref>

Starbreeze intended for ''Escape from Butcher Bay'' to feature more complex [[Role-playing game (video games)|role-playing game]] systems, but feedback from Diesel and game testers dissuaded them. Starbreeze senior producer Peter Wanat said, "We tried to limit the number of really hard or really intricate RPG elements, and that was a choice because we wanted the game to be playable."<ref name="ignsbint2" /> Other removed features include an electric [[bullwhip]] for the guard Abbott, and a 25-minute final [[Boss (video games)|boss]] fight.<ref name="ignsbint6" /><ref name="ignsbint7">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-pt-2?page=4|title=Epilogue: The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay, Pt. 2|last=Perry|first=Douglass C.|page=4|date=September 2, 2004|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160311075105/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/02/epilogue-the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-pt-2?page=4|archive-date=March 11, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> A [[PlayStation 2]] version that was in development was cancelled so the company could focus on the Xbox version.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.1up.com/features/starbreeze-secret-history?pager.offset=2 |title=Inside Starbreeze:The Secret History of the Riddick Team |page=3 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160524135552/http://www.1up.com/features/starbreeze-secret-history?pager.offset=2 |archive-date=May 24, 2016 |work=[[1UP.com]] |publisher=Ziff Davis |last=Leone |first=Matt |date=June 2, 2011 |access-date=June 3, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The game uses [[normal mapping]], which allows detailed textures to be drawn on models with lower [[Polygon (computer graphics)|polygon]] counts; this increases visual fidelity, without sacrificing higher [[frame rate]]s.<ref name="gspyxboxreview2">{{cite web|url=http://xbox.gamespy.com/xbox/the-chronicles-of-riddick/520233p2.html|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review|last=Williams|first=Bryn|page=2|date=June 1, 2004|publisher=GameSpy|access-date=April 6, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090416060756/http://xbox.gamespy.com/xbox/the-chronicles-of-riddick/520233p2.html|archive-date=April 16, 2009|url-status=live}}</ref> It also featured dynamic lighting with per-pixel [[stencil shadowing]] and [[self-shadowing]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/a_chroniclingriddickpart2|title=Chronicling Riddick: Journey To Butcher Bay|last=Bramwell|first=Tom|date=June 9, 2004|publisher=Gamer Network Ltd.|access-date=November 22, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130518065254/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/a_chroniclingriddickpart2|archive-date=May 18, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Escape from Butcher Bay'' was completed in 18&nbsp;months.<ref name="ignsbint" /> Vin Diesel promoted the game and the accompanying movie at the May 2004 [[Electronic Entertainment Expo]] (E3) video game convention.<ref name="igne3">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/05/14/riddick-rules-e3|title=Riddick Rules E3|last=D.|first=Spence|date=May 14, 2004|work=IGN|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104011508/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/05/14/riddick-rules-e3|archive-date=November 4, 2012|url-status=live}}</ref> The game was released in North America on June 1, 2004, shortly before ''The Chronicles of Riddick''.<ref name="gspotships">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-ships/1100-6099681/|title=Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay ships|last=Thorsen|first=Tor|date=June 1, 2004|work=GameSpot|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131205224158/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-ships/1100-6099681/|archive-date=December 5, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> North American [[pre-order]]s of the game included a [[DVD]] of promotional content, such as a partial interactive [[Strategy guide|walkthrough]] and footage from the film.<ref name="gipreorder">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.gameinformer.com/News/Story/200405/N04.0524.1755.37334.htm|title=Chronicles Of Riddick Pre-Order Bonus Announced|last=Cook|first=Chris|date=May 24, 2004|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|publisher=[[GameStop]]|access-date=April 5, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050223090624/http://www.gameinformer.com/News/Story/200405/N04.0524.1755.37334.htm|archive-date=February 23, 2005}}</ref> The game's soundtrack, composed by [[Gustaf Grefberg]], was released by Vivendi as a free download on June 24, 2004.<ref name="gspotmusic">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/riddick-game-soundtrack-available-for-free/1100-6101370/|title=Riddick game soundtrack available for free|last=Thorsen|first=Tor|date=June 24, 2004|work=GameSpot|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131206065405/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/riddick-game-soundtrack-available-for-free/1100-6101370/|archive-date=December 6, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

Following rumors, Vivendi confirmed in July 2004 that a [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]] [[Porting|port]] of ''Escape from Butcher Bay'' was in development, entitled "''The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Director's Cut''".<ref name="gzsales">{{cite web |date=October 15, 2004 |title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay – Developer's Cut Announced |url=http://www.gamezone.com/news/10_15_04_01_56PM.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090330051339/http://www.gamezone.com/news/10_15_04_01_56PM.htm |archive-date=March 30, 2009 |access-date=March 31, 2009 |publisher=GameZone}}</ref> The game features a higher [[display resolution]], additional cigarette packs, and new scenes where Riddick steals mechanized riot armor. It includes developer commentary which details the game's creation and design decisions.<ref name="ignpcreview" /> The game was released on December 8 in North America.<ref name="gspydcut">{{cite web|url=http://pc.gamespy.com/pc/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay/557571p1.html|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay -Developer's Cut Announced|last=Van Autrijve|first=Rainier|date=October 15, 2004|publisher=GameSpy|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090430101204/http://pc.gamespy.com/pc/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay/557571p1.html|archive-date=April 30, 2009|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Expanded remake===
{{Quote box|align=right|width=23%|"We're very happy to be working in the Riddick universe again.  ''Assault on Dark Athena'' gives us an opportunity to revisit the original game and share it with a new audience, as well as offer a continuation of the ''Butcher Bay'' gameplay and storyline."|— Ian Stevens, Starbreeze Studios<ref name="gsutraathena" />}}
{{main|The Chronicles of Riddick: Assault on Dark Athena}}
In May 2007, Vivendi announced that ''Escape from Butcher Bay'' was being [[Enhanced remake|remade]] by Starbreeze Studios for PC, [[Xbox 360]] and [[PlayStation 3]]. Entitled ''The Chronicles of Riddick: Assault on Dark Athena'', the game was referred to by Vivendi as a "reinvention" of ''Escape from Butcher Bay''; it would include a multiplayer mode and new single-player content.<ref name="gsutraathena">{{cite web|url=http://gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=14032|title=Vivendi Confirms Xbox 360/PS3 Riddick Remake|last=Jenkins|first=David|date=May 22, 2007|website=Gamasutra|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090417092208/http://gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=14032|archive-date=April 17, 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref>  It was planned that Vivendi-subsidiary [[Sierra Entertainment]] would publish the game in late 2007.<ref name="gspotathena">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/news/6171213.html|title=Chronicles of Riddick redux confirmed for '07|date=May 21, 2007|publisher=CBS Interactive|author=Gamespot Staff|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071014102049/http://www.gamespot.com/news/6171213.html|archive-date=October 14, 2007|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="gsutraannounce">{{cite web|url=http://gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=21007|title=Atari Confirmed As New Ghostbusters Publisher|last=Jenkins|first=David|date=November 7, 2008|website=Gamasutra|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090417092323/http://gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=21007|archive-date=April 17, 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In December 2007, [[Activision]] and Vivendi Games [[Mergers and acquisitions|merged]] to become [[Activision Blizzard]];<ref name="gspotmerger">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/news/6183557.html|title=Vivendi merges with Activision in $18.9B deal|last=Thorsen|first=Tor|date=December 2, 2007|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090407064244/http://www.gamespot.com/news/6183557.html|archive-date=April 7, 2009|url-status=live}}</ref> the new company announced the dismissal of ''Assault on Dark Athena'', ''[[Brütal Legend]]'', ''[[Ghostbusters: The Video Game]]'' and others from its roster in July 2008. The titles were put up for sale to other publishers.<ref name="gspotstream">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/news/6195105.html|title=Activision Blizzard 'streamlining' Vivendi|last=Sinclair|first=Brendan|date=July 28, 2008|website=GameSpot|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090407064413/http://www.gamespot.com/news/6195105.html|archive-date=April 7, 2009|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="gspotdrop">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/news/6195113.html|title=Brutal Legend, Ghostbusters, more dropped by Activision|last=Sinclair|first=Brendan|date=July 28, 2008|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090407033023/http://www.gamespot.com/news/6195113.html|archive-date=April 7, 2009|url-status=live}}</ref> In September 2008, Starbreeze Studios confirmed that the game was still in development, and that it was nearing completion.<ref name="gspotdone">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/news/6198151.html|title=Dark Athena 'just about done'|last=Magrino|first=Tom|date=September 24, 2008|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090418043038/http://www.gamespot.com/news/6198151.html|archive-date=April 18, 2009|url-status=live}}</ref> The following month, Atari reportedly paid a flat fee for the publishing rights to ''Assault on Dark Athena'' and ''[[Ghostbusters: The Video Game]]'';<ref name="gsutrareport">{{cite web|url=http://gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=20879|title=Report: Atari To Publish Ghostbusters, Riddick|last=Jenkins|first=David|date=October 30, 2008|website=Gamasutra|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090417092318/http://gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=20879|archive-date=April 17, 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> Atari later confirmed that it had picked up both titles.<ref name="gsutraannounce" /> The company also stated that it had struck a deal with [[Universal Pictures|Universal Studios]] to develop more ''Chronicles of Riddick'' games.<ref name="variety">{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2008/digital/markets-festivals/atari-gets-riddick-ghostbusters-1117994909/|title=Atari gets 'Riddick,' 'Ghostbusters'|last=Fritz|first=Ben|date=October 29, 2008|publisher=Reed Business|access-date=April 5, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090417082325/http://www.variety.com/article/VR1117994909.html?categoryid=1079&cs=1|archive-date=April 17, 2009|url-status=live}}</ref>  ''Assault on Dark Athena'' was released in April 2009 in North America, Europe, and Australia.<ref name="palgnannounce">{{cite web|url=http://palgn.com.au/article.php?id=13720&sid=322d90172fea6a8059355878fc0ccb77|title=Assault on Dark Athena release date announced|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110526133139/http://palgn.com.au/xbox-360/13720/assault-on-dark-athena-release-date-announced/|archive-date=May 26, 2011|last=Rositano|first=Joseph|date=February 24, 2009|website=PALGN|access-date=April 5, 2009}}</ref>

''Escape from Butcher Bay'' received critical acclaim.<ref name="gamerankingspc"/><ref name="gamerankingsxbox"/><ref name="mcpcscore" /><ref name="mcxboxscore" /> Certain reviewers preferred the game over its film counterpart, and considered it an exception to the general mediocrity of film [[tie-in]] games.<ref name="gspotxboxreview" /><ref name="fsquadpcreview">{{cite web|url=http://www.firingsquad.com/games/riddick_butcher_bay_review/|title=Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130421011922/http://www.firingsquad.com/games/riddick_butcher_bay_review/|archive-date=April 21, 2013|last=Wojnarowicz|first=Jakub|date=January 7, 2005|work=PC|publisher=FiringSquad|access-date=April 2, 2009}}</ref><ref name="ceathenaqa">{{cite news|url=http://cincinnati.metromix.com/movies/article/the-chronicles-of-riddick/943664/content|title='The Chronicles of Riddick' video game Q&A|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120220020953/http://cincinnati.metromix.com/movies/article/the-chronicles-of-riddick/943664/content|archive-date=February 20, 2012|last=Semel|first=Paul|date=February 9, 2009|newspaper=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]]|access-date=April 14, 2009}}</ref>

name="ignpcreview2">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/12/14/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-developers-cut?page=2|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay-Developer's Cut Review|page=2|last=Perry|first=Douglass C.|author2=Adams, Dan|date=December 14, 2004|work=PC|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 2, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107012956/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/12/14/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-developers-cut?page=2|archive-date=November 7, 2012|url-status=live}}</ref> and to stealth game series like ''[[Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell|Splinter Cell]]'',<ref name="gproxboxreview">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.gamepro.com/article/reviews/36050/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay/|title=Review: The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Gear]]'',<ref name="cvgxboxreview" /> and ''[[Thief (series)|Thief]]''.<ref name="fsquadpcreview2">{{cite web|url=http://www.firingsquad.com/games/riddick_butcher_bay_review/page2.asp|title=Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111214001210/http://firingsquad.com/games/riddick_butcher_bay_review/page2.asp|archive-date=December 14, name="euroxboxreview" /><ref name="ignpcreview" /> ''[[Game Informer]]'''s Jeremy Zoss noted that "every aspect of play is expertly implemented",<ref name="ginformerxboxreview" /> and ''[[GameSpot]]''{{'}}s [[Greg Kasavin]] believed that the game "effectively and innovatively combines excellent shooting, hand-to-hand combat, stealth, and adventure elements".<ref name="gspotpcreview" /> While the game's stealth mechanics were praised,<ref name="euroxboxreview" /><ref name="fsquadpcreview2" /> certain critics received its first-person shooter elements with less enthusiasm.<ref name="ignpcreview2" /><ref name="gspypcreview2" /> Reviewers applauded the control scheme, such as the Xbox version's [[analog stick]]-based hand-to-hand combat.<ref name="gspotxboxreview2">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay/reviews/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-review-6099643/?page=2|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review for Xbox|page=2|last=Kasavin|first=Greg|date=June 1, 2004|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 2, 2009}}</ref><ref name="euroxboxreview" /><ref name="ginformerxboxreview" /><ref name="ignpcreview2" /> The implementation of Riddick's [[Riddick (character)#Eyeshine|eyeshine]] ability was also generally praised,<ref name="fsquadpcreview2" /><ref name="gspotpcreview2">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay/reviews/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-developers-cut-review-6114822/?page=2|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review for PC|page=2|last=Kasavin|first=Greg|date=December 10, 2004|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 2, 2009}}</ref> but ''[[Computer and Video Games]]'' believed that it was no different from [[Night vision device|night vision goggles]] in other first-person shooters, and said that it "could've been developed into so much more."<ref name="cvgxboxreview" />

The game's visuals—particularly the Xbox version's—were acclaimed,<ref name="euroxboxreview" /><ref name="ginformerxboxreview">{{cite web|url=http://www.gameinformer.com/Games/Review/200407/R04.0719.1617.01533.htm|title=Chronicles of Riddick|work=Xbox|publisher=Game Informer|first=Jeremy|last=Zoss|access-date=April 2, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050209230530/http://www.gameinformer.com/Games/Review/200407/R04.0719.1617.01533.htm|archive-date=February 9, 2005 }}</ref><ref name="ewxboxreview">{{cite web|url=https://ew.com/article/2006/12/27/we-rate-chronicles-riddick-escape-butcher-bay-videogame/|title=We rate the {{sic|hide=y|reason=double 'the' error in source title}} "The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay" videogame|date=July 8, 2004|work=Xbox|publisher=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=April 14, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090416063127/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,661956,00.html|archive-date=April 16, 2009|url-status=live}}</ref> and compared to those of ''Doom 3'' and ''[[Half-Life 2]]''.<ref name="ginformerxboxreview" /><ref name="fsquadpcreview" /><ref name="gspypcreview2" /> ''GameZone''{{'}}s Michael Lafferty said that the game's graphics "[take] the genre to the next level".<ref name="gzxboxreview" /> The textures and lighting were cited as high points,<ref name="gzxboxreview" /><ref name="gspypcreview2">{{cite web|url=http://pc.gamespy.com/pc/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay/572714p2.html|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay - Director's Cut Review|page=2|last=Madigan|first=Jamie|date=December 13, 2004|work=PC|publisher=GameSpy|access-date=April 2, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090416061826/http://pc.gamespy.com/pc/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay/572714p2.html|archive-date=April 16, 2009|url-status=live}}</ref> particularly because of the gameplay role of shadows.<ref name="europcreview" /><ref name="fsquadpcreview3">{{cite web|url=http://www.firingsquad.com/games/riddick_butcher_bay_review/page3.asp|title=Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review|page=3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120928061043/http://www.firingsquad.com/games/riddick_butcher_bay_review/page3.asp|archive-date=September 28, 2012|last=Wojnarowicz|first=Jakub|date=January 7, 2005|work=PC|publisher=FiringSquad|access-date=April 2, 2009}}</ref> Character models and facial animations were considered highly realistic; much praise was given to those of Riddick.<ref name="gspotxboxreview3" /><ref name="cvgpcreview" /><ref name="europcreview" /><ref name="euroxboxreview" /> ''GameSpot'' appreciated the developers' attention to detail; they noted that recent bullet-holes glow red and smoke, but gradually cool and darken.<ref name="gspotxboxreview3">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay/reviews/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-review-6099643/?page=3|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review for Xbox - Page 3|page=3|last=Kasavin|first=Greg|date=June 1, 2004|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 2, 2009}}</ref> Certain reviewers complained about graphical glitches, such as "seams" and "clipping",<ref name="ignpcreview" /><ref name="ginformerxboxreview" /> and gave as an example the visibility of [[Tracer ammunition|bullet tracers]] through walls.<ref name="gspotpcreview" /> The portrayal of Butcher Bay was considered convincing, and ''[[1UP.com|1UP]]''{{'}}s Shawn Elliott compared it to the settings of the [[Alien (franchise)|''Alien'' franchise]].<ref name="1uppcreview" /><ref name="gspotxboxreview3" /><ref name="euroxboxreview" />
{{Blockquote|"You can almost smell the thick stink of Butcher Bay and its inhabitants from the grime on the walls, dirty clothes of the inmates, and environmental textures.  This place oozes with style and creates sense of reality in which it's easy to become immersed."|Perry and Adams, ''[[IGN]]''<ref name="ignpcreview">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/12/14/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-developers-cut|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay-Developer's Cut Review|page=1|last1=Perry|first1=Douglass C.|last2=Adams|first2=Dan|date=December 14, 2004|work=PC|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 2, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120823022030/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/12/14/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-developers-cut|archive-date=August 23, 2012|url-status=live}}</ref>}}
The audio of ''Escape from Butcher Bay'' was generally well received,<ref name="gzxboxreview" /><ref name="ignpcreview3" /> and critics praised its voice acting; the performances of Vin Diesel and Cole Hauser were given special commendation.<ref name="ginformerxboxreview" /><ref name="gspotpcreview3">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay/reviews/the-chronicles-of-riddick-escape-from-butcher-bay-developers-cut-review-6114822/?page=3|title=The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review for PC|page=3|last=Kasavin|first=Greg|date=December 10, 2004|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=April 2, 2009}}</ref><ref name="fsquadpcreview4">{{cite web|url=http://www.firingsquad.com/games/riddick_butcher_bay_review/page4.asp|title=Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay Review|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120928185353/http://www.firingsquad.com/games/riddick_butcher_bay_review/page4.asp|archive-date=September 28, 2012|page=4|last=Wojnarowicz|first=Jakub|date=January 7, 2005|work=PC|publisher=FiringSquad|access-date=April 2, 2009}}</ref> In regard to the music, FiringSquad's Jakub Wojnarowicz stated, "It's not good enough to sweep you away[,] but it's also not bad enough to stick out like a sore thumb".<ref name="fsquadpcreview3" /> ''IGN'' said, "The music isn't memorable, but it's not bad".<ref name="ignxboxreview5"/> The ''[[Sunday Herald Sun]]'' called the voice acting "Surprisingly good".<ref>{{cite news|title=Game of the week|author=Staff|newspaper=Sunday Herald Sun|location=Melbourne, Australia|date=August 22, 2004|page=F02}}</ref> The game's length was commonly criticized. Reviewers noted that it could be completed in eight to fifteen hours,<ref name="1uppcreview" /><ref name="ginformerxboxreview" /><ref name="ignpcreview3" /> and ''IGN'' said, "If you consider around 12 hours of gameplay short, then Riddick is just that."<ref name="ignpcreview3" /> Several reviewers were displeased by the game's lack of multiplayer components;<ref name="europcreview" /><ref name="gradarpcreview" /><ref name="ignpcreview3" /> ''Computer and Video Games'' referred to it as a "missed opportunity".<ref name="cvgpcreview" /> ''Game Informer'' said, "Since the main quest is short [...] and there is no multiplayer, it's not a ton of game for your money."<ref name="ginformerxboxreview" />

Professor [[James Paul Gee]], a researcher of video games, has used ''Escape from Butcher Bay'' in his studies. He discussed the relation of [[Garrett (character)|Garrett]] from ''[[Thief (series)|Thief]]'' and the nameless soldier from ''[[Full Spectrum Warrior]]'' with the character of Riddick, saying that the games "allow players to take a projective stance to the (virtual) world, but a stance that is rooted in the knowledge, values, and ways of seeing and being in the world of an authentic professional, an 'expert'."<ref>{{cite journal|citeseerx = 10.1.1.128.3508|first=James Paul |last=Gee|date=November 30, 2006|title=Pleasure, Learning, Video Games, and Life: The Projective Stance|journal=A New Literacies Sampler|volume=29|pages=107}}</ref>

=== Sales ===
The Xbox version of the game had sold 159,000 units by August 2004, and was among the best-selling games on any platform during June 2004;<ref name="gzsales" /><ref>{{cite magazine |last=Traiman |first=Steve |date=October 23, 2004 |title=Promos Pairs Games, DVD |magazine=Billboard |page=54}}</ref> it was later re-released as a [[Platinum Hits]] title.<ref name="xboxplatinum">{{cite web |title=Platinum Hits - First-Person Action |url=http://www.xbox.com/en-US/games/platinumhits/firstpersonaction.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090601181432/http://www.xbox.com/en-US/games/platinumhits/firstpersonaction.htm |archive-date=June 1, 2009 |access-date=April 5, 2009 |publisher=Xbox.com}}</ref> Conversely, the PC version sold 32,500 after six months on shelves.<ref name="cnnsales">{{cite web |last=Saltzman |first=Marc |date=June 18, 2005 |title=Top PC games can end up in bargain bin |url=http://edition.cnn.com/2005/TECH/fun.games/06/17/bargain.games/index.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090416103657/http://edition.cnn.com/2005/TECH/fun.games/06/17/bargain.games/index.html |archive-date=April 16, 2009 |access-date=March 31, 2009 |publisher=CNN}}</ref> 

In a December 2008 interview, Ian Stevens (Head of Tigon Studios) said that sales were lackluster because consumers were not "big on Vin Diesel" and "highly skeptical of a film property translating well as a video game".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2008-12-24 |title=Butcher Bay sold 'purely on word of mouth,' better than word of foot |url=https://www.destructoid.com/butcher-bay-sold-purely-on-word-of-mouth-better-than-word-of-foot/ |access-date=2023-07-29 |website=Destructoid |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Awards and accolades===
Both versions of the game were given editor's choice awards from ''IGN'',<ref name="ignxboxreview5" /><ref name="ignpcreview3" /> ''GameSpot'',<ref name="gspotxboxreview" /><ref name="gspotpcreview" /> and [[GameSpy]].<ref name="gspyxboxreview" /><ref name="gspypcreview" /> ''GameSpot'' named it the best Xbox game of June 2004,<ref name=gotm>{{cite web | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040806144142/http://www.gamespot.com/features/6101893/index.html | url=http://www.gamespot.com/features/6101893/index.html | title=''GameSpot''{{'}}s Month in Review for June 2004 | author=Staff | date=July 6, 2004 | work=[[GameSpot]] | archive-date=August 6, 2004 | url-status=dead }}</ref> and the PC version was ''IGN''{{'}}s PC Game of the Month for December 2004.<ref name="ignpcaward">{{cite web|url=http://pc.ign.com/articles/576/576858p1.html|title=Game of the Month: December 2004|author=IGN Staff|date=January 3, 2005|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 5, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110613155544/http://pc.ign.com/articles/576/576858p1.html|archive-date=June 13, 2011}}</ref> It later won ''GameSpot''{{'}}s annual "Most Surprisingly Good Game" and "Best Game Based on a TV or Film Property" awards, and was a runner-up in the publication's "Best Action Adventure Game", "Best Original Music", "Best Sound Effects", "Best Story", "Best Graphics, Technical", "Best Voice Acting" and "Most Innovative Game" categories, as well as for „Game of the Year”.<ref name=bestworst2004>{{cite web | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050307021607/http://www.gamespot.com/gamespot/features/all/bestof2004/ | url=http://www.gamespot.com/gamespot/features/all/bestof2004/ | title=Best and Worst of 2004 | date=January 5, 2005 | work=[[GameSpot]] | archive-date=March 7, 2005 | url-status=dead }}</ref> The editors of ''[[Computer Gaming World]]'' presented ''Butcher Bay'' with their 2004 "Action Game of the Year" award, and hailed it as "the best movie prequel ever produced".<ref name=cgwpremier2004>{{cite magazine | author=((Editors of ''CGW'' ))| magazine=[[Computer Gaming World]] | title=2004 Games of the Year |date=March 2005 | issue=249 | pages=56–67 }}</ref> ''[[Computer Games Magazine]]'' named ''Escape from Butcher Bay'' the tenth-best computer game of 2004.<ref name=cgm14th>{{cite journal | author=Staff | journal=[[Computer Games Magazine]] | title=The Best of 2004; The 14th Annual ''Computer Games'' Awards |date=March 2005 | issue=172 | pages=48–56 }}</ref>

''IGN'' later ranked ''Butcher Bay'' 12th on its list of the 25 greatest Xbox games of all time.<ref name="ign25">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2007/03/17/the-top-25-xbox-games-of-all-time?page=3|title=The Top 25 Xbox Games of All Time|page=3|last1=Perry|first1=Douglass C.|last2=Brudvig|first2=Erik|last3=Miller|first3=Jon|date=March 16, 2007|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=April 2, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120823002409/http://www.ign.com/articles/2007/03/17/the-top-25-xbox-games-of-all-time?page=3|archive-date=August 23, 2012|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Game Informer'' placed ''Escape from Butcher Bay'' as the 8th best on their list of 25 greatest Xbox games of all time.<ref>{{cite magazine |author=Game Informer Staff |year=2008 |title=Xbox Top 25 |magazine=Game Informer |issue=187 |pages=136–137}}</ref> ''Escape from Butcher Bay'' was nominated for ''GameSpot''{{'}}s Game of the Year award for 2004,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/gamespot/features/all/bestof2004/day6f_1.html |title=Best of 2004 Game of the year nominees |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105021048/http://www.gamespot.com/gamespot/features/all/bestof2004/day6f_1.html |archive-date=November 5, 2012 |publisher=CBS Interactive|author=Gamespot the year Winner|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130523122421/http://www.gamespot.com/gamespot/features/all/bestof2004/day6w_2.html|archive-date=May 23, 2013|publisher=CBS
